title: His Dark Materials: Why the Underrated Fantasy Saga Deserves a Sequel
text:
Explore why HBO's His Dark Materials, despite its critical acclaim and brilliant cast, didn't achieve the global popularity it deserved, and why a sequel could finally give it the recognition it merits.
Daemons and talking polar bears and a repressive religious regime, oh my! When it comes to vastly underrated fantasy sagas, it doesn't get much better than HBO's His Dark Materials.
Produced in collaboration with BBC One, the much-anticipated TV series based on Phillip Pullman's trilogy of novels is set in a multiverse that includes our own world. His Dark Materials follows young Lyra Belacqua (Dafne Keen) and her daemon Pantalaimon (Kit Connor) as they uncover a conspiracy involving kidnapped children and a mysterious cosmic substance known as Dust, teaming up with Will Parry (Amir Wilson), a boy from another world, to battle the authoritarian Magisterium.
Also starring James McAvoy and Lin-Manuel Miranda, His Dark Materials received critical acclaim for its outstanding cast and breathtaking visuals but, despite its success in the United Kingdom, didn't become quite as popular as the series deserved to be. Unfortunately, lack of worldwide mainstream appeal typically means that an IP is shelved.
But there is still so much more to explore in Pullman's and Lyra's world, and a sequel might be just what His Dark Materials needs to get the flowers it deserves. His Dark Materials' November 2019 premiere was an attempt to capitalize on the sudden fantasy TV series-shaped hole left by the end of Game of Thrones and its controversial final season.
But, despite positive reviews, the series struggled to stand out amidst a new host of adaptations also hoping to become the next big fantasy series, including House of the Dragon, The Witcher, and The Wheel of Time. The show's intricate plotting and philosophical underpinnings set it apart from more conventional fantasy fare, yet it never quite captured the global zeitgeist in the way its rivals did.
This is a shame because the series boasts a richly developed world, complex characters, and morally ambiguous themes that reward careful viewing. The performances, particularly Keen's portrayal of Lyra and McAvoy's Lord Asriel, are consistently excellent, and the visual effects bring Pullman's imagination to life with stunning clarity. From the frozen North to the bustling streets of Oxford, every location feels authentic and immersive, drawing viewers deeper into the story.
A sequel could build on these strengths and give the series the recognition it deserves. The source material offers ample material for future seasons, as Pullman has expanded his universe with The Book of Dust trilogy, which explores Lyra's later adventures and the origins of Dust. Bringing this story to the screen would not only satisfy existing fans but also introduce a new generation to Pullman's thought-provoking narrative.
Moreover, the cultural landscape has shifted since the show first aired, with audiences increasingly hungry for stories that challenge simple good-versus-evil dichotomies. His Dark Materials tackles issues like religious fundamentalism, the abuse of power, and the importance of free will, making it more relevant than ever. A revival or sequel could ride this wave of renewed interest, positioning itself as a mature alternative to the more formulaic fantasy shows currently on the air.
So let's hope that the powers that be recognize the untapped potential of Lyra's world and greenlight a follow-up. In a genre crowded with dragons and swords, His Dark Materials offers something genuinely different, and it's time it got the spotlight it always deserved
